character_generation_blueprint.LEVEL_PLACEMENT: Place the character on the scale of 1 to 100 described by LEVEL_BANDS, by what the backstory says they can do today. 1 is an ordinary person of this world; 100 is a legend.
character_generation_blueprint.USE_THE_ROSTER: When a roster of existing characters with their levels is given, place the new character relative to them: who they could face, outmatch or be outmatched by. The roster is the saga's own scale; the bands are only the first reference.
character_generation_blueprint.NO_FREE_INFLATION: A character is not strong because they are important. A villain revealed late may enter very high, but only if the backstory supports it.
character_generation_blueprint.LEVEL_RATIONALE: levelRationale is one line: why this level, pointing at the backstory or at a character in the roster.
character_generation_blueprint.SKILLS_LIST: skills is a short list of the abilities the character has today, as brief noun phrases. It replaces the abilities text fields.

unified_lore_generation_blueprint.CHARACTER_STATUS: For each character whose situation changed in this stretch of story, set status: ACTIVE, ABSENT (alive and away from the scene, reachable), MISSING or DEAD. Leave it out when nothing changed.
unified_lore_generation_blueprint.STATUS_NOTE: statusNote is a short phrase when nuance matters ('jailed in the North Tower', 'travelling north'). A jailed character who can still appear in a scene stays ACTIVE.
unified_lore_generation_blueprint.STATUS_REASON: Every status change needs statusReason: the event that caused it, in one line.
unified_lore_generation_blueprint.DEAD_IS_RARE: Mark DEAD only when the story shows it plainly, never because a character is out of the scene or presumed lost. When in doubt, MISSING.
unified_lore_generation_blueprint.STATUS_RETURNS: Moving a DEAD character back to another status needs a clear reason in the story (a spirit, a resurrection, a mistaken report).

reply_generation_blueprint.POWER_CONTEXT_IS_BINDING: POWER_CONTEXT gives the level gap between the characters in the scene. In a contest of the dimension at stake (combat, skill, authority) the gap decides the outcome: narrate a clear advantage as a clear advantage and never invent difficulty to keep the scene tense. It does not decide emotional scenes.
reply_generation_blueprint.STATUS_GATES_PRESENCE: A character with status DEAD only appears as a memory, a flashback or a spirit. A MISSING or ABSENT character does not walk into a scene without a reason the story gives.
